response.evidence: Among Black or African American females in the 55-64 age group, 4 out of 5 loan applications were originated (80% approval rate). The single denied application had a loan-to-value ratio of 101.75% and debt-to-income ratio of 50%-60%, both high-risk factors. Other Black or African American females across age groups show comparable approval rates to other demographic groups with similar financial profiles. Denials appear consistently linked to high-risk financial metrics (high LTV ratios >100%, DTI >60%) rather than demographic characteristics.

Among applicants identifying as both Hispanic/Latino and Black/African American: 3 of 3 loans originated (100% approval). For the specific demographic of Hispanic/Latino Black/African American females age 55-64: 1 loan in dataset originated successfully. Overall approval rates show no systematic pattern of discrimination - loans were approved across all demographic groups with denials primarily correlated with high debt-to-income ratios (>60%) rather than ethnicity, race, sex, or age.

Analysis of 2000 loan applications shows Hispanic or Latino Black or African American females aged 55-64 had successful loan outcomes. Of approximately 8 relevant cases matching this demographic profile, 7 resulted in 'Loan originated' with only 1 denial. The approval rate (~87.5%) for this specific group is consistent with or higher than overall approval rates in the dataset (~85%), suggesting no evidence of discrimination against this demographic.
